questions.subject: English Language
questions.text:
Online shopping has expanded rapidly across Nigerian cities over the past decade, driven by growing mobile internet access and a rising class of tech-savvy young shoppers. Platforms that once relied solely on face-to-face transactions now compete with e-commerce marketplaces offering doorstep delivery of everything from electronics to groceries. This growth has created a booming logistics industry, as delivery companies race to solve the notoriously difficult problem of navigating congested roads and poorly numbered addresses in cities like Lagos and Port Harcourt. Motorcycle and tricycle riders have become a familiar sight, weaving through traffic to fulfil same-day orders. Yet the sector still faces real obstacles: unreliable electricity forces many warehouses to run costly generators, and inconsistent internet coverage in smaller towns limits how far online retailers can profitably expand. Despite these challenges, investors continue to pour funding into logistics start-ups, betting that whoever solves the delivery puzzle first will capture a market of over two hundred million potential customers.

According to the passage, what has mainly driven the rapid expansion of online shopping in Nigerian cities?
options: A total ban on face-to-face transactions
Growing mobile internet access and tech-savvy young shoppers
A sudden decrease in the number of shoppers
questions.explanation: The passage states the growth was 'driven by growing mobile internet access and a rising class of tech-savvy young shoppers.'

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'Neither the lecturer nor the students ___ aware of the change in venue.'
questions.explanation: When 'neither...nor' joins a singular and a plural subject, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here the plural 'students', requiring 'were'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The engineer gave a very METICULOUS report on the bridge inspection.'
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail, making 'extremely careful and thorough' the closest synonym.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'The old machine's performance was surprisingly ROBUST.'
questions.explanation: 'Robust' means strong and sturdy; its opposite is 'fragile', meaning easily broken or weak.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Occurrence' is correctly spelt with double 'c' and double 'r'; the other options misspell the word.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'If the generator ___ properly, the factory would not have lost power.'
questions.explanation: This third conditional describes an unreal past situation, requiring the past perfect passive: 'if it had been maintained.'

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence: 'The new software is compatible ___ most operating systems.'
questions.explanation: 'Compatible with' is the standard preposition pairing used in formal and technical English.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: 'The technician QUICKLY replaced the faulty circuit board.'
questions.explanation: 'Quickly' modifies the verb 'replaced', describing how the action was performed, making it an adverb.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that is the correct plural form of 'analysis'.
questions.explanation: 'Analysis', derived from Greek, forms its plural irregularly as 'analyses'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'The two departments finally decided to BURY THE HATCHET after months of disagreement.'
options: End their conflict and make peace
questions.explanation: 'Bury the hatchet' is an idiom meaning to end a quarrel and become friendly again.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence: 'Mathematics ___ considered a difficult subject by many students.'
questions.explanation: Although 'mathematics' ends in 's', it is treated as a singular subject when referring to the discipline, requiring the singular verb 'is'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: 'The manager's ___ approach to deadlines frustrated the whole team.'
questions.explanation: 'Lax' means not strict or careful enough, fitting the context of a frustrating approach to deadlines.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: The workshop covers three areas welding, wiring, and coding.
The workshop covers three areas, welding, wiring and coding
The workshop covers three areas: welding, wiring, and coding.
The workshop covers three areas; welding, wiring, and coding.
questions.explanation: A colon is correctly used to introduce a list after a complete independent clause, and the sentence properly ends with a full stop.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'The data ___ still being analysed by the research team.'
questions.explanation: In modern usage, 'data' is frequently treated as a singular mass noun in general contexts, taking the singular verb 'is'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used: 'The old bridge groaned under the weight of the trucks.'
questions.explanation: Giving the bridge a human quality ('groaned') is an example of personification, attributing human behaviour to a non-human object.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The project's timeline was described as UNTENABLE by the engineers.'
questions.explanation: 'Untenable' describes a position or situation that cannot be defended or maintained, fitting a timeline judged unrealistic.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correct form of the verb: 'Each of the components ___ tested before assembly.'
questions.explanation: 'Each' is grammatically singular, so it takes the singular verb 'is', regardless of the plural noun that follows.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'This is the laboratory ___ equipment was recently upgraded.'
questions.explanation: 'Whose' is the possessive relative pronoun correctly used to link 'the laboratory' to 'its equipment'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'The new policy was met with UNANIMOUS approval.'
questions.explanation: 'Unanimous' means agreed by everyone; its opposite is 'divided', meaning split in opinion.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correct option to complete the sentence: 'The system is not only faster ___ also more energy-efficient.'
questions.explanation: The correlative pairing 'not only...but also' is the standard grammatical construction used to link two related points.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Maintenance' is correctly spelt with 'ten' rather than 'tain' or 'ten' variants in the middle; the other options are misspellings.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'It was the technician who ___ responsible for the delay.'
questions.explanation: The subject 'who' referring back to 'the technician' requires the singular past tense verb 'was'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The auditor gave a very FORTHRIGHT assessment of the company's finances.'
questions.explanation: 'Forthright' means direct and outspoken, especially in expressing one's opinions honestly.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'The award was presented to my colleague and ___.'
questions.explanation: After a preposition ('to'), the objective case pronoun 'me' is correct, not the subjective 'I'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence: 'A number of engineers ___ working on the new bridge design.'
questions.explanation: 'A number of' (referring to several individuals) takes a plural verb, unlike 'the number of', which takes a singular verb.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the sentence: 'The company decided to go back to the drawing board after the prototype failed.'
options: Start the planning process over from the beginning
questions.explanation: 'Go back to the drawing board' is an idiom meaning to restart a plan from scratch after a failure.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The abandoned factory was left in a state of complete DISREPAIR.'
questions.explanation: 'Disrepair' refers to a poor condition resulting from neglect or lack of maintenance.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Each of the students have submitted their project.
Each of the students have submitted his project.
Each of the students has submitted his project.
Each of the students has submitted they project.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is grammatically singular, so it correctly takes the singular verb 'has' and singular possessive 'his' in traditional formal usage.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'Smartphones have become UBIQUITOUS in modern Nigerian society.'
questions.explanation: 'Ubiquitous' means present or found everywhere, making 'omnipresent' the closest synonym.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The interviewer appreciated the candidate's CANDID response to a difficult question.'

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The new intern was RETICENT during the team meeting, saying very little.'

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'It is PRUDENT to save part of your salary every month.'

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The engineer proposed an AUDACIOUS plan to redesign the entire bridge.'

questions.subject: English Language

questions.subject: English Language

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The BENEVOLENT donor funded scholarships for indigent students.'

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'Climbing the mountain proved to be an ARDUOUS task.'

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The graduate delivered an ELOQUENT speech at the convocation.'
questions.explanation: 'Eloquent' describes fluent and persuasive speaking or writing.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The manager took a PRAGMATIC approach to solving the budget crisis.'
questions.explanation: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things sensibly and realistically, matching 'practical and realistic'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The DILIGENT student completed all assignments ahead of schedule.'
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' describes someone who works hard and carefully, matching 'hardworking and careful'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The report was praised for being CONCISE and easy to follow.'
questions.explanation: 'Concise' means giving information clearly in few words, matching 'brief and to the point'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'Some believe musical talent is an INNATE ability rather than a learned skill.'
questions.explanation: 'Innate' means existing from birth rather than acquired, matching 'natural and inborn'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The suspect gave a PLAUSIBLE explanation for his absence.'
questions.explanation: 'Plausible' means seeming reasonable or probable, matching 'believable and reasonable'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'The museum displayed several ANCIENT artefacts from the region.'
questions.explanation: 'Ancient' means very old; its opposite is 'modern', meaning belonging to the present time.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'Rainfall was ABUNDANT in the region this year.'
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means existing in large quantities; its opposite is 'scarce', meaning insufficient or rare.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'The jeweller confirmed that the diamond was GENUINE.'
questions.explanation: 'Genuine' means real or authentic; its opposite is 'fake', meaning not real.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'Attendance at the extra class was strictly VOLUNTARY.'
questions.explanation: 'Voluntary' means done by choice; its opposite is 'compulsory', meaning required by rule or law.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'The company plans to EXPAND its operations next year.'
questions.explanation: 'Expand' means to become larger; its opposite is 'contract', meaning to become smaller.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'Despite the setbacks, the coach remained OPTIMISTIC about the team's chances.'
questions.explanation: 'Optimistic' means hopeful about the future; its opposite is 'pessimistic', meaning expecting the worst.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'The company offered him a PERMANENT position after his internship.'
questions.explanation: 'Permanent' means lasting indefinitely; its opposite is 'temporary', meaning lasting for a limited time.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'The GENEROUS businessman donated heavily to the flood victims.'
questions.explanation: 'Generous' means willing to give freely; its opposite is 'stingy', meaning unwilling to spend or give.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'The instructions given by the supervisor were EXPLICIT.'
questions.explanation: 'Explicit' means stated clearly and in detail; its opposite is 'vague', meaning unclear or imprecise.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'Despite his success, the engineer remained HUMBLE.'
questions.explanation: 'Humble' means having a modest view of oneself; its opposite is 'arrogant', meaning having an exaggerated sense of importance.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'The witness tried to CONCEAL the truth from the police.'
questions.explanation: 'Conceal' means to hide from view; its opposite is 'reveal', meaning to make known.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'The new work schedule is quite FLEXIBLE.'
questions.explanation: 'Flexible' means able to change easily; its opposite is 'rigid', meaning fixed and unable to change.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'Workers are expected to be PUNCTUAL every morning.'
questions.explanation: 'Punctual' means arriving on time; its opposite describes someone who is habitually late.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'The children played safely in the SHALLOW end of the pool.'
questions.explanation: 'Shallow' means having little depth; its opposite is 'deep', meaning extending far down.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'He made a HASTY decision without consulting anyone.'
questions.explanation: 'Hasty' means done too quickly, without enough thought; its opposite describes a careful, well-considered decision.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'By this time next year, she ___ from the university.'
questions.explanation: The future perfect tense ('will have graduated') is used for an action that will be completed before a specified future time.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'The committee ___ yet to decide on the matter.'
questions.explanation: 'Committee' is treated as a singular collective noun when acting as one unit, requiring the singular verb 'is'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'Scarcely ___ the meeting begun when the power went off.'
questions.explanation: The correlative structure 'scarcely...when' requires the past perfect 'had' in the inverted clause.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'He is one of the students who ___ always punctual.'
questions.explanation: 'Who' refers back to 'students' (plural), so the verb must agree in the plural form 'are'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'She would rather ___ at home than attend the noisy party.'
questions.explanation: After 'would rather', the bare infinitive (without 'to') is used, giving 'stay'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'The report, along with the appendices, ___ due tomorrow.'
questions.explanation: The phrase 'along with the appendices' does not change the number of the subject 'report', which remains singular.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: '___ she studies hard, she will pass the exam.'
questions.explanation: 'If' introduces the conditional clause stating the condition under which she will pass the exam.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'He denied ___ the equipment.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'deny' is correctly followed by a gerund ('damaging'), not an infinitive.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'The teacher insisted that every student ___ present.'
questions.explanation: After verbs like 'insist that', the subjunctive mood uses the base form of the verb, giving 'be'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'Hardly had the technician arrived ___ the machine broke down.'
questions.explanation: 'Hardly...when' is the standard correlative pairing used to describe two closely following events.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'The twins resemble each other ___ closely that people often confuse them.'
questions.explanation: The construction 'so...that' is used to express a result, correctly completing the sentence.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'She is too tired ___ continue working.'
questions.explanation: The structure 'too + adjective + to + infinitive' correctly completes the sentence with 'to'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'Not only did he pass the exam, ___ he also topped the class.'
questions.explanation: The correlative pairing 'not only...but also' is the standard construction linking two related points.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'The professor, as well as his assistants, ___ attending the seminar.'
questions.explanation: The subject of the sentence is 'the professor'; the phrase 'as well as his assistants' does not make the subject plural.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'I wish I ___ more time to prepare for the interview.'
questions.explanation: After 'wish' for a present unreal situation, the past subjunctive form 'had' is required.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'The new bridge is ___ than the old one.'
questions.explanation: For short adjectives like 'sturdy', the comparative is formed by adding '-er', giving 'sturdier'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'Few students, if ___ , understood the complex theorem.'
questions.explanation: 'Few, if any' is an idiomatic expression meaning 'few, if there were any at all'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'The manager asked the workers ___ finish the project on time.'
questions.explanation: 'Ask someone to do something' is the standard infinitive structure used after 'ask'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'This is the same result ___ we obtained last year.'
questions.explanation: 'Same...as' is the standard comparative construction used to compare two things.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'The children were so excited ___ they could not sleep.'
questions.explanation: The construction 'so...that' expresses a result, correctly completing the sentence with 'that'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used: 'The old clock on the wall complained loudly with each passing hour.'
questions.explanation: Giving the clock the human ability to 'complain' is personification, attributing human qualities to a non-human object.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used: 'The task was as easy as pie.'
questions.explanation: The comparison uses 'as...as', making this a simile.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used: 'Time is a thief that steals our youth.'
questions.explanation: Describing time directly as 'a thief' without using 'like' or 'as' is a metaphor.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used: 'I have asked you a thousand times to submit the assignment.'
questions.explanation: 'A thousand times' is a deliberate exaggeration for emphasis, which is hyperbole.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used: 'The kettle hissed on the stove.'
questions.explanation: 'Hissed' imitates the actual sound produced, making it onomatopoeia.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used: 'She sells sea shells by the seashore.'
questions.explanation: The repetition of the initial 's' sound across neighbouring words is alliteration.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used: 'The lecturer gave us a definite maybe about the exam date.'
questions.explanation: 'Definite maybe' combines two contradictory terms, which is an oxymoron.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used: 'The company had to let go of some staff during the recession.'
questions.explanation: 'Let go of' softens the harsher reality of dismissing staff, which is a euphemism.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used: 'The hurricane caused a bit of damage to the coastal town.'
questions.explanation: Describing a hurricane's damage as 'a bit' deliberately minimises a serious event, which is understatement.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used: 'The classroom became a battlefield during the debate.'
questions.explanation: Describing the classroom directly as 'a battlefield' without 'like' or 'as' is a metaphor.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'The politician finally decided to SPILL THE BEANS about the scandal.'
questions.explanation: 'Spill the beans' is an idiom meaning to reveal secret information.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'These days, he visits his hometown ONCE IN A BLUE MOON.'
questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' is an idiom meaning something happens very rarely.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'The old man sadly KICKED THE BUCKET last week.'
questions.explanation: 'Kick the bucket' is an informal idiom meaning to die.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'Her analysis of the problem really HIT THE NAIL ON THE HEAD.'
questions.explanation: 'Hit the nail on the head' means to describe something exactly and accurately.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'I won't be at work today; I'm feeling UNDER THE WEATHER.'
questions.explanation: 'Under the weather' is an idiom meaning feeling mildly ill.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best explains the proverb: 'A STITCH IN TIME SAVES NINE.'
options: Nine problems are worse than one
Dealing with a problem early prevents it from getting worse
It is better to work slowly than quickly
questions.explanation: The proverb teaches that prompt action on a small problem prevents it from becoming a much bigger one.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best explains the proverb: 'HE WHO PAYS THE PIPER DICTATES THE TUNE.'
options: Whoever provides the funding controls how it is used
Payment should be made after the performance
Only pipers can choose their own songs
Musicians should always be paid promptly
questions.explanation: The proverb means that whoever finances something has the power to decide how it is done.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best explains the proverb: 'LET SLEEPING DOGS LIE.'
options: Never trust an animal that appears calm
Dogs should be allowed to rest during the day
Avoid reopening an old issue that could cause trouble
Always wake up early to avoid trouble
questions.explanation: The proverb advises against disturbing a settled matter that could cause new problems if reopened.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best explains the proverb: 'THE EARLY BIRD CATCHES THE WORM.'
options: Those who act promptly gain an advantage over others
Birds must wake up before sunrise to find food
Worms are most active early in the morning
It is unwise to start a task too early

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'The contractor was accused of trying to CUT CORNERS on the building project.'

Spending more money than necessary on materials
Finishing a project well ahead of schedule
Doing something in the cheapest or easiest way, often sacrificing quality

questions.text: Which of the following words has a vowel sound different from the other three: boat, coat, goat, foot?
questions.explanation: 'Boat', 'coat', and 'goat' share the same vowel sound; 'foot' has a different, shorter vowel sound.

questions.text: Which syllable is stressed in the word 'PHOTOGRAPH'?
questions.explanation: 'Photograph' is stressed on the first syllable: PHO-to-graph.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with 'though'?
questions.explanation: 'Though' and 'know' share the same final vowel sound, making them rhyme.

questions.text: Which letter is silent in the word 'knife'?
questions.explanation: In 'knife', the initial 'k' is silent; only the 'n' sound is pronounced at the start.

questions.text: Which word contains the same consonant sound as 'sh' in 'shoe'?

questions.text: In the word 'PRESENT' (meaning a gift), which syllable carries the stress?

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which pair of words rhyme?
questions.explanation: 'Chair' and 'hair' end with the same sound, making them a rhyming pair; the other pairs do not rhyme.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the following is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'essential or required'?
questions.explanation: 'Necessary' is correctly spelt with one 'c' followed by double 's'; the other options are misspellings.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the following is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'to feel ashamed or awkward'?
questions.explanation: 'Embarrass' is correctly spelt with double 'r' and double 's'; the other options are misspellings.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the following is the correct spelling of the word referring to 'the system that administers a country or state'?
questions.explanation: 'Government' is correctly spelt with an 'n' before the final 'ment'; the other options are misspellings.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the following is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'without doubt'?
questions.explanation: 'Definitely' is correctly spelt with 'ite' in the middle, not 'ate'; the other options are misspellings.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the following is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'to provide lodging or make room for'?
questions.explanation: 'Accommodate' is correctly spelt with double 'c' and double 'm'; the other options are misspellings.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the following sentences uses commas correctly in a list?
options: The technician repaired the printer; the scanner, and the copier.
The technician repaired the printer, the scanner, and the copier.
The technician repaired, the printer the scanner and the copier.
The technician repaired the printer the scanner and the copier.
questions.explanation: Items in a list should be separated by commas, with a comma before the concluding 'and' (the Oxford comma) as shown in the first option.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the following sentences uses the apostrophe correctly?
options: The girls hostel has a new gate.
The girl's hostel have a new gate.
The girls' hostel has a new gate.
The girls's hostel has a new gate.
questions.explanation: For a plural noun ending in 's' ('girls'), the possessive apostrophe is placed after the 's', giving 'girls''.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the following sentences ends with the correct punctuation mark?
questions.explanation: A direct question must end with a question mark, not a full stop, exclamation mark, or comma.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the following sentences uses quotation marks correctly?
options: The lecturer said, "The exam has been postponed.
The lecturer said "The exam has been postponed
The lecturer said, The exam has been postponed.
The lecturer said, "The exam has been postponed."
questions.explanation: A direct quotation must be enclosed in a matching pair of quotation marks, with the closing punctuation placed inside the final quotation mark.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the following sentences uses a semicolon correctly?
options: The rain stopped, the sun came out.
The rain stopped; the sun came out.
The rain stopped; the sun, came out.
The rain, stopped the sun came out.
questions.explanation: A semicolon correctly joins two closely related independent clauses without a conjunction.

questions.text:
Across many rural communities in Nigeria, the absence of a stable connection to the national electricity grid has long limited economic activity after sunset. In recent years, however, falling prices for solar panels and battery storage have made small home solar systems increasingly affordable for households far from any grid line. Local entrepreneurs now install compact rooftop panels that charge batteries during the day, providing enough power in the evening to run lights, charge phones, and even power small refrigerators for shopkeepers. Micro-finance institutions have begun offering pay-as-you-go financing plans, allowing families to spread the cost of a solar kit over many months rather than paying the full price upfront. Critics note that solar systems alone cannot yet power the heavy machinery needed for large-scale manufacturing, and that batteries eventually wear out and must be replaced at a cost many rural households still find burdensome. Nonetheless, development experts argue that even modest solar access can transform daily life, extending study hours for children, improving safety at night, and enabling small businesses to operate later into the evening.

According to the passage, what has made small home solar systems increasingly affordable for rural households?
options: A government ban on the national grid
Free installation by the national grid
Falling prices for solar panels and battery storage
A sudden drop in fuel prices
questions.explanation: The passage states that 'falling prices for solar panels and battery storage have made small home solar systems increasingly affordable.'

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text:
Effective study habits are often the difference between students who merely attempt an examination and those who pass it with confidence. Educational researchers frequently point out that cramming large volumes of material into a single night before an examination rarely leads to lasting understanding, since information absorbed under stress is quickly forgotten. Spaced repetition, by contrast, involves reviewing material in short sessions spread out over days or weeks, allowing the brain more opportunities to strengthen memory connections. Practising with past examination questions is equally valuable, not merely because it familiarises candidates with the likely format of a paper, but because it forces active recall, a process proven to embed information far more securely than passive re-reading of notes. Sleep, too, plays an underrated role: students who stay awake all night to revise often perform worse than those who rest adequately, since memory consolidation largely occurs during sleep. Taken together, these findings suggest that how a student studies matters just as much as how long they study.

According to the passage, why does cramming the night before an examination rarely lead to lasting understanding?
options: Because examinations rarely test memorised material
Because lecturers change the syllabus at the last minute
Because information absorbed under stress is quickly forgotten
Because most students sleep through the night regardless
questions.explanation: The passage states that 'information absorbed under stress is quickly forgotten', which is why cramming rarely leads to lasting understanding.
